sources.entry: Harbor - Open-source download manager for HTTP(S), magnet links, and .torrent files. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/thsnkhn/harbor) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.one_liner: Harbor is a free, open-source, native SwiftUI download manager for macOS that handles direct HTTP(S) downloads, public media links, magnet links, and .torrent files.
summary.what_it_does: Harbor is a macOS app built with SwiftUI for downloading direct HTTP and HTTPS files, public media links with previews and video or audio format selection, and magnet links or local .torrent files. Torrents can be previewed so you choose which files to fetch before starting. Batch add lets you paste many links, pick one folder, and queue them together. It offers traffic profiles (Unlimited, Balanced, Quiet, Custom), global and per-download speed limits, torrent watch folders, seeding controls, and share-ratio limits. Queues persist across launches, with pause, resume, retry, cancel, and history, plus Finder reveal, open-file actions, and Quick Look previews for completed downloads. A Safari extension hands links to Harbor through the harbor:// and magnet: URL schemes, and a harbor://download?url=... scheme lets other tools open the Add Download sheet.
use_cases: download files on a Mac with a native app
download torrents or magnet links on macOS
batch queue many download links into one folder
download public videos or audio with format selection
hand off links from Safari to a download manager
limit download bandwidth on a Mac
how_to_run: Or download the latest DMG from the project and drag Harbor.app into Applications
stack: yt-dlp (offered for recognized pages such as YouTube)
notable: Native SwiftUI macOS interface with sidebar, unified toolbar, and detail inspector
Safari extension intercepts clicks on download links and magnet links, with a per-site toggle
Torrent preview lets you pick files before downloading
Local-first: no accounts, sign-in, hosted backend, or subscriptions
harbor:// URL scheme for browser extensions, CLIs, and automations
caveats: Safari extension is an approximation: it only sees link clicks, not script-started, form-post, or redirected downloads
Downloads requiring sign-in may fail because Harbor fetches URLs without Safari's cookies or session
Safari extension setup needs manual steps, including allowing the extension and 'Other websites' access; local unsigned builds require developer settings and ad hoc signing
keywords: download links from browser to mac app
